title: mTLS namespace RBAC sync
content:
Meeting: mTLS + namespace RBAC sync (architecture review)
Date: 2026-03-11 10:00am PT
Location: Zoom / #platform-arch channel
Attendees: Priya, Daniel, Asha, Marco, Jia (plus notes from SRE async)
Purpose: review proposed design for tightening service-to-service authentication and namespace-scoped RBAC for the platform control plane and customer workloads. We need a design that: enforces mTLS on all internal RPCs, maps platform identities to namespace RBAC policies, supports private deployments (VPC/on-prem), and enables a safe rollout with fallbacks.
---
Summary decision (proposed, pending final signoff):
- Adopt a hybrid approach: require mTLS for all platform control-plane RPCs by default; allow operator-configurable permissive-mode for a short staged rollout.
- Implement namespace-scoped RBAC via an admission controller + centralized policy engine (OPA/wasm) that evaluates requests using certificate SAN (service identity) and namespace metadata.
- Use short-lived service certs issued by the internal CA (SPIRE prototype) with automated rotation.
Rationale: this balances strong mutual auth with a practical migration path for Dedicated/Private where operators may need a permissive window. Using OPA as the central policy evaluator keeps rules flexible and enables existing teams to author policies in Rego.
---
Problems we're solving:
1) Unauthenticated/unauthorized control-plane calls between microservices (e.g., model registry -> scheduler) observed in some test clusters.
2) Customer workload isolation: ensure actions affecting a customer namespace cannot be performed by services not authorized for that namespace.
3) Compliance for Private customers: must support local CA/HSM integrations and offline rotation.
---
Options considered (short):
A) Enforce network-only isolation + kube RBAC (current baseline).
  - Pros: low friction; fits existing infra.
  - Cons: insufficient for mTLS auth, pod-to-pod identity spoof risk.
B) Full service mesh (Envoy+mTLS, Istio-style) across all clusters.
  - Pros: mature mTLS + telemetry, policy hooks.
  - Cons: heavy operational cost, hard for private/on-prem customers; mesh upgrades are risky.
C) Lightweight mTLS + admission-time namespace RBAC (recommended hybrid).
  - Pros: lower infra footprint, compatible with private deployments, leverages SPIRE for cert management and OPA for policy.
  - Cons: we must build some glue (admission controller + policy sync) and add rollout tooling.
---
Design sketch (high level):
1) Identity issuance: use SPIRE (or pluggable CA adapter) to mint node/service certs; SAN contains service identity and namespace label (when applicable). Certificates are short-lived (12h–24h) with automatic rotation agent. For Private installs allow swap-in of local CA/HSM via KMS provider interface.
2) Transport: mTLS enforced at gRPC layer for control-plane RPCs. Each server will validate peer cert SAN and fingerprint against expected service identities. For languages without native mTLS support, provide thin proxy sidecar library (lightweight) or TLS-enabled envoy listener.
3) Authorization: admission controller intercepts Kubernetes API and internal control-plane requests. Central policy engine (OPA wasm) consumes: service identity, namespace, action, resource. Policies sourced from platform repo and per-tenant policy overlays.
4) Rollout modes:
   - permissive (initial): server validates certs but logs failures and allows request.
   - strict: server rejects non-mTLS connections.
   - audit-only policy mode for RBAC: policy decisions logged and flagged before enforcement.
5) Fallbacks: if CA unavailable, auto-fallback to permissive for <15 mins with operator alerts; for private installs, fallback uses local CA certs configured at bootstrap.
---
Telemetry / observability:
- Add per-request labels: peer_identity, namespace, policy_decision.
- Platform Console will surface mTLS error rates and policy violation counts per-namespace.
- Integrate with existing tracing hooks and token-level cost dashboards for correlation.
---
Security review notes:
- Validation: ensure SAN cannot be spoofed; restrict SPIRE spiffe IDs to pre-approved workload registration entries.
- Threat: compromised node may mint certs if registration is too permissive. Mitigation: require attestation (K8s node identity + signed bootstrap token).
- Private deployments: document HSM CA integration steps and ensure offline rotation is supported.
---
Migration plan (phased):
Phase 0 (2 wks): prototype in staging. Implement SPIRE + small e2e: cert issuance, gRPC mTLS handshake, logging.
Phase 1 (3 wks): permissive rollout in non-critical clusters. Enable audit logs, collect failures, update policies.
Phase 2 (4 wks): enable strict mTLS for control-plane core services (model-registry, scheduler, router) behind feature flag. Rollout with canary subset of clusters.
Phase 3 (2–4 wks): admission controller + OPA policy enforcement for namespace-scoped actions.
Phase 4 (ongoing): harden for Private installs (HSM integration, docs), and GA.
Notes: timelines assume 2 engineers from platform + 1 SRE part-time. Dedicated/Private customer pilot timelines may be longer.
---
Action items (owner / due):
- Priya: finalize SPIRE vs internal CA evaluation doc; include HSM integration checklist. Due: 2026-03-19
- Daniel: prototype gRPC mTLS handshake and failure logging (staging). Due: 2026-03-18
- Asha: draft Rego policy templates for namespace isolation + admin roles; add example testcases. Due: 2026-03-22
- Marco: instrument telemetry hooks to include peer_identity and policy_decision. Due: 2026-03-25
- Jia: update deployment runbook with permissive->strict toggle and rollback steps. Due: 2026-03-20
---
Open questions / risks:
- How do we represent multi-tenant overlays when a single platform service legitimately needs cross-namespace access (e.g., billing exporter)? Recommend explicit allowlist via policy with expiring tokens.
- Can we reuse any existing cert rotation agents used by Dedicated infra, or is SPIRE adoption required? (Priya to research existing agents).
- Performance: admission controller + OPA per-request latency — need bench targets (<5ms median added). Marco to run microbench.
- Operator UX for Private: how do we surface cert rotation status and HSM errors without leaking secrets? Design required.
---
Docs and next steps:
- Create focused RFC (short) capturing the hybrid approach + rollout schedule; include conformance tests and perf targets. (Priya)
- Schedule follow-up architecture review (2 weeks) to review prototype results and policy templates.
- Add a customer-facing one-pager for Dedicated/Private customers describing the security model and migration expectations.
---
Notes to self / informal reminders:
- Keep permissive window as short as possible; add automatic escalation if error rates stay high.
- Reuse existing policy repos and adopt semantic versioning for policy bundles so we can roll back bad rules.
- Consider an emergency bypass token for SRE during initial strict rollout (audit logged + time-limited).

End of notes.
